class.name: PlayerController
class.brief_description: Controller for the local player: possesses a pawn and owns its input.
class.description: On possession it makes the pawn camera current and calls [code]_setup_input_component[/code] on the [PawnHandler], which is where input actions get bound. It belongs to a level and dies with it. The human behind it is the [LocalPlayer], which the [GameInstance] owns and which survives [method GFGDSceneTree.open_level] - that is where the device assignment and the split screen viewport live. [method get_player_input] is the shortcut to the player own action state; without a [LocalPlayer] it returns [code]null[/code] and the [InputComponent] falls back to the global [Input] singleton.

method.name: get_player_state
method.description: Lives under the [GameState], not under this node.

method.name: get_player_viewport
method.description: [member LocalPlayer.viewport_override] if the player has one, otherwise this node viewport.

method.name: is_local_player_controller
method.description: Always true today. The hook exists so code written now stays correct once a client owns only a subset of the world controllers.

method.name: register_input_component
method.description: Adds the component to this controller input stack and points it at this controller, which is how it finds the right [PlayerInput].
